title: Samuel Listens to God
subtitle: A boy heard his name in the night three times before he knew who was calling
mainTruth: God speaks, and the right answer is: 'Speak, Lord — I am listening.'

read.title: Read Together
read.text:
There was a woman called Hannah who wanted a baby very much and had waited a long time. She prayed and prayed, and God gave her a son. She called him Samuel, and because she was so thankful, she gave him back to God — when he was still small, he went to live and serve at God's house with an old priest called Eli.

Now in those days, the Bible says, God did not speak to people very often. It was a quiet time.

One night Samuel was lying down to sleep, and the lamp in God's house was still burning. And he heard a voice call his name: 'Samuel!'

Samuel jumped up and ran to Eli, because who else could it be? 'Here I am — you called me.' But Eli said, 'I did not call you. Go back and lie down.' So he did.

Then it happened again. 'Samuel!' And again Samuel ran to Eli. And again Eli said, 'I did not call you, my son. Go and lie down.'

And a third time. 'Samuel!' And a third time Samuel got up and went.

Then Eli understood. He said, 'Go and lie down, and if He calls you again, say this: Speak, Lord — for Your servant is listening.'

So Samuel went back. And the Lord came and stood there and called, 'Samuel! Samuel!'

And Samuel said, 'Speak — for Your servant is listening.'

God gave Samuel a message that night, and it was a hard one about Eli's family. In the morning Samuel was afraid to tell Eli — but he told him the truth anyway, all of it. And Samuel grew up, and God was with him, and everybody came to know that Samuel really did hear from God.

He was only a boy. But he listened, and he obeyed, and he told the truth even when it was hard.
read.childText: Hannah wanted a baby for a long time. God gave her a son called Samuel, and she thanked God by giving him back to God. So Samuel lived at God's house with an old priest called Eli. One night Samuel heard someone call his name. He ran to Eli — but Eli said, 'I did not call you.' It happened again. And again! The third time, Eli understood and said, 'If He calls again, say: Speak, Lord — Your servant is listening.' So God called, 'Samuel! Samuel!' And Samuel said, 'Speak — Your servant is listening.' God gave him a hard message, and Samuel told the truth anyway. He was only a boy!

discuss.title: Talk About It
discuss.question: What did Samuel say when he knew it was God?
discuss.parentGuide: Responsive hearing is the concept: God speaks and we answer 'I am listening'. Two useful notes for your child. Samuel did not recognise God's voice at first and needed an older person to help him — needing help to hear God is normal, not a failure. And listening led straight to a hard job he was afraid of, which he did anyway; obedience is what proves listening. Say plainly that today God speaks to us mainly through the Bible, so 'listening to God' means reading and obeying it, not waiting for a voice at night. Retrieve Deborah: God uses the willing, including the very young.
discuss.familyQuestion: What makes it hard to listen properly?

pray.title: Let's Pray
pray.guidedPrayer: God, thank You that You speak to us in the Bible. Help us to be quiet enough to listen, and brave enough to do what You say — even the hard parts. Speak, Lord. We are listening. Amen.
pray.childPrompt: Can you say to God: 'Speak, Lord — I am listening'?
prayerPoints: Tell God you want to listen to Him
Ask God for courage to obey the hard parts

remember.title: Remember This
remember.memoryVerse: Samuel said: 'Speak, Lord. Your servant is listening.'
remember.tip: Turn all the lights down, sit very still, and whisper it three times: 'Speak, Lord, I'm listening.' Cup a hand behind your ear each time.

doToday.title: Do It Today
doToday.action: Listen to a grown-up all the way to the end today without interrupting once — then do what they said.
doToday.parentNote: Listening is a skill before it is a virtue, and interrupting is developmentally normal at this age, so aim for one deliberate success rather than a whole day. Give them your own undivided listening in return — it teaches far more than the instruction.
